newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - T-bonds to pause before 110-06 challenge.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - T-bonds to pause before 110-06 challenge.

text.p: T-bond futures may take a breather at current highs, or pull back a bit, before Friday's key payrolls data provides new guidelines, technical analysts said.
The September contract is on Wednesday faced with the tough challenge of breaking above a major down trendline that comes in at 110-06, and the important high of 110-09 set on May 13.

Ian Stannard, technical analyst at Chase in London, said before the payrolls the market might not have the stamina to fight the trendline. "A corrective pull back from here in the very near term isn't surprising," he said.
At 1000 GMT, T-bonds were 3/32 down at 110-00.
Earlier on Wednesday, T-bonds extended the rally to test the trendline, which has been in place since December, but stalled just one tick shy of it and retreated back.
"It is a very, very important trendline," Stannard noted.

But if the trendline, and 110-09, fell then the recovery trend that developed from the 105-30 low in April would be extended towards the upper boundary of that channel, providing an upside target at 111-03/111-05, Stannard said.
Support came in at 109-31 on intraday charts, followed by the 109-27/26 congestion area, Tuesday's low of 109-20 and Monday's low of 109-12.
Tom Hobson, director of technical analysis at Merrill Lynch in London, said failing to move above 110-09 on Wednesday, T-bonds would stall and head back on Thursday.
"But today I would approach it with a positive outlook," he said.
"Essentially the market remains unchanged -- there's a positive short-term tone there after last week's rebound and that should continue to support the market up until Friday."
Hobson placed modest support around the mid-May congestion area of 109-10, but more importantly from 108-30 up to 109-00.
At 1040, September Eurodollars were steady at 94.015.
